recognize_zh: 透過目鏡拍攝的低倍血液抹片中，紅血球之間有一條細長、呈彎曲鉤狀、染成紫色的線狀蟲體，長度相當於數十個紅血球，即為微絲蚴（microfilaria）。
features: Single elongated, slender, coiled/hook-shaped worm many red-cell diameters long lying among red cells
Purple-staining body with a column of nuclei suggested but not individually resolved at this magnification
Tapering tail at one end and a curved looped anterior portion
Sheath, cephalic space and tail-tip nuclei cannot be assessed at this low magnification
Background red cells without obvious intraerythrocytic parasites
describe_en: Low-power photomicrograph of a peripheral blood smear, taken through the eyepiece, shows a single elongated, coiled, purple-staining nematode larva measuring many red-cell diameters in length, lying among red cells. The body tapers toward one end; sheath characteristics and the arrangement of tail nuclei cannot be evaluated at this magnification. No other parasites are identified in the field. Findings are consistent with microfilaremia; species identification requires high-power examination of the sheath and tail nuclei (e.g., Wuchereria bancrofti versus Brugia malayi) on a Giemsa-stained thick film, ideally collected at night.

ddx.dx: Wuchereria bancrofti vs Brugia malayi vs Loa loa
ddx.vs: Separation relies on high-power features: W. bancrofti is sheathed with a nucleus-free tail tip, Brugia has two separate terminal tail nuclei, and Loa loa has nuclei extending to the tail tip.
Mansonella microfilariae are smaller, unsheathed and have a blunt tail with nuclei to the tip.
Artifacts are refractile, of uniform thickness without tapering ends or internal nuclear column.
Trypanosomes are only about 2-3 red cells long with an undulating membrane, flagellum and kinetoplast.
